clue.text: Some dog-ends, say, for animal painter

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to hear how the words for dog-ends are spoken

parts.note: dog-ends are cigarette stubs, the butts left over

explanation.surface: Somebody collects cigarette butts on behalf of a painter of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sound: STUBS (dog-ends) is pronounced like the painter's name. George Stubbs was the eighteenth-century English painter famous for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs is the celebrated English painter of horses and other creatures.

clue.text: Historical romance writer partly seen as a bat in innings after innings

explanation.walkthrough: The name runs through 'aS A BAT IN Innings'; 'after innings' only fills out the cricket picture. Rafael Sabatini wrote Scaramouche and Captain Blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafael Sabatini was an Italian-British novelist of swashbuckling historical romances such as Scaramouche.

explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to release or let go, just as letting slip means setting free.

explanation.definitionFit: Théophile Gautier was a nineteenth-century French poet, novelist and critic.

explanation.definitionFit: The word means necessities or requirements, as earning and writing were for O'Brien.

clue.text: Transitory occasional pieces of Nabokov — or objects of his hobby?
